weather-fetch.note: Declared network access must not be treated as exfiltration.

config-checker.note: Reading a declared project configuration file must not be flagged.

evasion._comment: Evasion cases in tests/fixtures/evasion. Each states what a good scanner should do. A case with known_gap is one the deterministic checks miss today: the test is a strict xfail, so it fails loudly when the gap closes (remove known_gap then). None is a known gap right now. Cases are scanned with the benign mock model, so only the deterministic stages can catch them. See docs/security/evasion-limits.md.

control-plain.note: Unobfuscated curl|bash. The baseline every evasion below is a variation of.

string-concat.note: The command is built from string parts; the os.system call is what the anchors see.

base64-split.note: A base64 payload split over lines, joined and exec'd; the decode-and-exec call is caught.

indirect-call.note: getattr(__import__('o'+'s'), 'sys'+'tem'); the anchors still see dynamic import and a curl|sh string.

table-injection.note: An injection in row 47 of a 70-row markdown table.

homoglyph.note: A Cyrillic letter in 'curl'. Caught since the checks also match a normalised form of each line (lookalike letters mapped to Latin).

split-download-exec.note: One file downloads to /tmp, another runs it. Caught by the cross-file check (download-then-exec), which names both places.

fullwidth-forms.note: Full-width letters in a curl|bash line; folded by NFKC.

invisible-chars.note: Zero-width characters inside curl and bash; dropped before matching.

greek-in-script.note: A Greek alpha in 'bash' in a shell script.

split-download-exec-shell.note: The same split in shell, with the destination in a variable.

split-download-exec-node.note: The same split in Node: https.get plus createWriteStream, then child_process.

split-bundled-flags.note: curl -sSLo FILE and wget -qO FILE: the file-taking letter is last in a bundle of short options.

split-attached-value.note: curl -o/tmp/p.sh: the value is attached to the option.

split-same-line-variable.note: D=/tmp/w; curl ... -o $D/z.sh: the variable is set on the same line as the download.
